text:
maria: quick follow-up on the RFC — i sketched an 'entry sieve' for model submissions. goal: catch obvious runtime/compat/quality regressions fast, without running full bench for every upload. thoughts?

alex: +1 to the idea. main worry is false negatives if the quick checks are too small. we shouldn't block a valid model because of noisy heuristics. :thinking:

jin: propose two-stage flow: (1) <quick-probe> lightweight fuzz + interface checks (30s), (2) <shadow-deep> forked deep bench during low-traffic hours. quick-probe decides immediate reject/accept for manual review.

jin: quick-probe parameters i had in mind: samples=50, max_len=256, check-kv-warmup, token-stability delta. something like:

```
bin/probe --model $ID --samples 50 --max-len 256 --seed 42 --budget 30s
```

sajid: agree on two-stage. metric proposal: perplexity ratio vs baseline, token-stability (ED on top-1 tokens), and a small suite of golden prompts that we keep curated per-arch. if perplexity_ratio > 1.5 or token-stability < 0.85 flag as flaky.

kevin: KV cache warming will be a pain for long-seq LMs. quick-probe should emulate a few warmup prefixes; otherwise latency regressions are invisible until runtime. also, some quantized binaries reorder weights and fail our simple loader — need an interface sanity check early.

lina: ops/telemetry note: mark quick-probe runs with "entry_sieve" tag and store: p50/p95 token latency, tokens-per-second, cost-estimate. for flagged models we should auto-schedule a canary route with 0.1% traffic to gather real traffic signals before full rollout.

maria: good call on canary. also thinking about an "opt-out heavy-eval" flag for models under active dev to avoid cost churn, but default should be opt-in. devs can request full bench manually.

alex: what about reproducibility? if quick-probe is non-deterministic across infra, we'll get noise. set seed + fixed runtime env (quantization params + kernel set) for the probe. maybe snapshot the runner image we used.

jin: agree. snapshotting runner image is cheap and helps us triage. add an artifact: probe-report.json with run config and small sample outputs + checksums.

eng-prober-bot: smoke-run complete for model "glassfinch-3b-quant" — 3 checks failed: interface-loader, kv-warmup, golden-prompt-x mismatch. logs: https://internal.logs/abc123 (truncated) :warning:

kevin: can someone paste the interface-loader error? that one usually indicates model export mismatch.

eng-prober-bot: interface-loader: "unexpected tensor shape (0,512) vs expected (1,512)".

sajid: that shape error usually means batch-dim handling in exporter. we should add a small lint in the ingest step that runs a shaped-forward with batch=1 and batch=2. quick but catches 90% of exporter slipups.

lina: ops question: do we want the entry_sieve to be synchronous on upload (blocking) or async with an "accept provisional" state? blocking is cleaner but hurts iteration velocity.

maria: lean toward async provisional accept + short TTL (48h) where model is available only for devs and not user-facing routes. if quick-probe fails during that window, auto-unpublish.

alex: that balances safety and velocity. also add an escalation path: one-click request for expedited deep bench if model owner thinks probe is false positive.

jin: implementation notes: reuse prober infra, ship a light binary in the upload runner, store probe artifacts in S3 shard keyed by model-id+probe-hash. add a scheduled nightly deep-bench runner for provisional models.

maria: next steps: i'll draft a short follow-up doc with the two-stage flow, metrics, and the provisional state UX. @lina can you stub telemetry tags? @kevin can you add batch-dim lint to exporter checklist? @sajid @jin please enumerate the golden-prompt set candidates. i'll circulate by EOD. :thumbsup:

alex: sounds good. can we add a line about fail-open for paid-tier customers? enterprise might want faster acceptance with manual review checkbox.

maria: yes — add routing policy override for enterprise. thanks everyone.

lina: noted, will post telemetry stub in #eng-ml later today.

kevin: i'll add the lint PR tomorrow.

sajid: compiling golden prompts now, will share sample matrix.

maria: closing loop: rough timeline — prototype in 2 sprints, prod rollout guarded by feature flag. :rocket:
